timeline.message:
Remove `assertAcked()` from `updateMinMasterNodes()`

When we're removing nodes there's a possibility for the cluster state
update to succeed but acking to fail (e.g. if it was waiting for an ack
from a removed node). Really there's no need to check for the acking of
the update here, we're in Zen2-land already.
timeline.author: David Turner

timeline.body:
When we're removing nodes there's a possibility for the cluster state
update to succeed but acking to fail (e.g. if it was waiting for an ack
from a removed node). Really there's no need to check for the acking of
the update here, we're in Zen2-land already.

Closes #96072

The test failure stack traces are certainly clear about the problem
```
  at org.hamcrest.MatcherAssert.assertThat(MatcherAssert.java:18)
  at org.elasticsearch.test.hamcrest.ElasticsearchAssertions.assertAcked(ElasticsearchAssertions.java:103)
  at org.elasticsearch.test.hamcrest.ElasticsearchAssertions.assertAcked(ElasticsearchAssertions.java:91)
  at org.elasticsearch.test.InternalTestCluster.updateMinMasterNodes(InternalTestCluster.java:2418)
  at org.elasticsearch.test.InternalTestCluster.excludeMasters(InternalTestCluster.java:2131)
  at org.elasticsearch.test.InternalTestCluster.stopNodesAndClients(InternalTestCluster.java:1995)
  at org.elasticsearch.test.InternalTestCluster.stopNodesAndClient(InternalTestCluster.java:1991)
  at org.elasticsearch.test.InternalTestCluster.stopCurrentMasterNode(InternalTestCluster.java:1905)
....
```
The code changes look good to me to address the shutdown / node departure problem. As to whether it is safe to disable assertAcked for all cluster state updates, per your mention of Zen2, I don't have enough context on that aspect. So Ievgen will need to sign off or I'll need some explanation / pointers.

I am a bit confused.

This says zen2 is default, however the actual constant value is `zen`:

https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/bcfbf000748b538884087623113682165abcb92d/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/discovery/DiscoveryModule.java#L63-L72

Anyways, even if it is using the different discovery type, is it safe to ignore ack?
The property is still used in couple of places as for 7.17, such as https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/bcfbf000748b538884087623113682165abcb92d/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/gateway/Gateway.java#L44

reply.body:
`zen` means Zen2, there is no option in 7.x to use the legacy discovery type.

Yes I believe this is safe, or at least it's no less safe than other things related to upgrading from 6.x. Which was never completely safe anyway.

timeline.body:
> disable assertAcked for all cluster state updates

NB we're only dropping it for the update which adjusts `discovery.zen.minimum_master_nodes`, which is a no-op in 7.x anyway - it only exists here because IIRC it's needed to support a rolling upgrade from 6.x, or a simulation of that case in an otherwise-7.x-only `InternalTestCluster`, but in the 5+ years since 7.x has been out I don't think we've seen any problems related to acking this update in those cases either.
